chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said:

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr, Abū Ṣidām, and a group spoke after the passing of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) about what was in the hands of the agents, and they wanted to investigate. So al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr came to Abū al-Ṣidām and said, “I intend hajj (pilgrimage).” Abū Ṣidām said to him, “Delay it this year.” Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr said to him, “I am alarmed in my sleep, and I must depart.” He made a bequest to Aḥmad ibn Yaʿlā ibn Ḥammād, and bequeathed wealth to the Nāḥiyah, and instructed him not to release anything except from his hand to his hand after his appearance.

He said: al-Ḥasan said, “When I arrived in Baghdād, I rented a house and stayed in it. Then one of the agents came to me with garments and dīnārs and left them with me. I said to him, ‘What is this?’ He said, ‘It is what you see.’ Then another came to me with the like of it, and another, until they filled the house. Then Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq came to me with all that he had with him. I was amazed and remained thinking, then a note from the man (عليه السلام) came to me: ‘When such-and-such of the day has passed, carry what is with you.’”

“So I departed and carried what was with me. On the road there was a vagabond highwayman with sixty men, but I passed by him and Allah kept me safe from him. Then I arrived at al-ʿAskar and lodged there. Then a note came to me: ‘Carry what is with you.’ So I packed it in the loads of the porters. When I reached the vestibule, there was a black man standing there. He said, ‘Are you al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Enter.’”

“So I entered the house and entered a room and unloaded the porters’ packs. In a corner of the room there was much bread, and each of the porters was given two loaves, and they were sent out. Then there was a room with a curtain over it, and I was called from it: ‘O Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr, praise Allah for what He has bestowed upon you, and do not doubt, for Shayṭān would dearly love that you should doubt.’ Then two garments were brought out to me, and it was said, ‘Take them, for you will need them.’ So I took them and departed.”
Saʿd said: “Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr returned, and he died in the month of Ramaḍān, and he was shrouded in the two garments.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبَيْنِ: the two garments later used as his shroud
key_terms.الْحَجَّ: hajj (pilgrimage) intended by al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرَ: al-ʿAskar, the military quarter associated with the Imam’s residence
key_terms.الْفَحْصَ: investigation or examination into the matter under discussion
key_terms.الْوُكَلَاءِ: the agents entrusted with handling the Imam’s affairs and funds
key_terms.رُقْعَةُ: a written note or signed message conveying instruction
key_terms.ظُهُورِهِ: his appearance or manifestation after concealment

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Imam’s hidden guidance and the transfer of wealth through his agents after the passing of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an episode after the passing of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), concerning property held by the agents and the hidden authority of the Imam. It describes al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr receiving instructions, safely delivering entrusted wealth, hearing a reassurance against doubt, and later being shrouded in the very garments he had been given. The report highlights trust in the Imam, the functioning of the wakālah network, and a sign connected to the Imam’s ghaybah and appearance.
